column1: # Docker Compose counters (compose.yaml, docker-compose.yml and their overrides), for a rule with
# the prompt file-body-ops: one per line, label TAB pattern (Java regex). The [ignore] line blanks
# YAML comments and the body of a block scalar (the lines below a | or > that are deeper than its
# key, past a list item's dash, as deep as the first of them; the key stays, and an empty command: >
# blanks no sibling key), so a key quoted in a command does not count. A service counts by the image: or
# build: it runs, so "services with an image" and "services built here" together are the services
# (one with both counts in each); the other keys count wherever they stand (a service's volumes: and
# the top-level volumes: alike). "variable substitutions" counts every ${NAME} and $NAME, not the
# escape $${NAME} or $$NAME, which Compose writes as a literal ($$${NAME} is a $ and a substitution).
# Compose interpolates a block scalar too (command: > with sh -c "echo ${GREETING}"), so that counter
# reads the file as written ([raw]) and leaves out only a $ in a comment: after a # at a line start or
# after a blank, at most 200 characters before it on its line.
# OpsFactPatternsTest pins every case; ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that every pattern reads linearly.
